issues.legal_issue: The filing of an arbitral award by the arbitrators is not barred by a limitation period that applies to applications made by parties.
material_facts: The arbitrators filed the award in court after it was made and notified the parties of the award.
The objection relied on a limitation provision governing applications by parties.
issues.conclusion: The award’s filing by the arbitrators was not barred by limitation because Article 178 of the Limitation Act applied to applications made by parties, not to filing by arbitrators.
issues.legal_principle: Article 178 of the Limitation Act, 1908, applies to applications made by parties and does not govern the filing of an award by arbitrators.

predicates.arbitration_award_proceeding: The proceeding concerns an award made in an arbitration.
predicates.arbitrators_filed_award: The arbitrators filed the award in court.
predicates.limitation_objection_based_on_party_appl: A party objected to filing on the basis of a limitation rule for applications made by parties.

issues.definition: When arbitrators file an award in an arbitration proceeding and the limitation objection concerns applications made by parties, the arbitrators’ filing is not barred by that limitation rule.

issues.legal_issue: An award that requires registration may nevertheless be filed in court before registration, but it cannot then be used as evidence to affect covered immovable property.
material_facts: The award was unregistered when the arbitrators first filed it in court.
The parties accepted that the award required registration.
The award was later registered and refiled.
issues.conclusion: Filing an unregistered award was not prohibited by section 49 of the Registration Act, although the award could not be taken into evidence so as to affect immovable property covered by section 17.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 17 and 49 of the Registration Act, 1908, require registration for the relevant award to affect immovable property, but section 49 does not prohibit filing the unregistered award in court; it restricts its evidentiary use to affect such property.

predicates.arbitration_award_proceeding: The proceeding concerns an award made in an arbitration.
predicates.award_requires_registration: The award requires registration to affect the relevant immovable property.
predicates.award_filed_before_registration: The award was filed in court before it was registered.

issues.definition: When an award requiring registration is filed in an arbitration proceeding before registration, the filing is permitted, although the award cannot be used as evidence to affect the covered immovable property.

issues.legal_issue: A registration challenge does not invalidate an award’s registration where the property particulars said to be missing were not necessary in the circumstances.
material_facts: The award was presented for registration without a separate list and particulars of the property.
A list and particulars were later supplied by an attorney for two of the arbitrators.
The High Court found that a property list was not necessary in the circumstances.
issues.conclusion: The absence of the list when the award was first presented did not invalidate its registration because the list was not necessary in the circumstances.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 21 and 22 of the Registration Act, 1908, and rules made under section 22 require property descriptions in applicable cases; where the description was not necessary in the circumstances, its later supply did not affect the legality of registration.

predicates.arbitration_award_proceeding: The proceeding concerns an award made in an arbitration.
predicates.award_registration_challenged_for_missin: A party challenged registration because property particulars were absent or supplied later.
predicates.property_particulars_not_required_in_cir: The circumstances did not require a separate list or particulars of the property for registration.

issues.definition: When registration of an arbitral award is challenged for missing property particulars that were not required in the circumstances, the registration is not invalidated for that reason.

issues.legal_issue: The court competent to entertain the filing of an award may extend the time for the arbitrators to make it.
material_facts: The arbitrators applied to the court for more time to make the award.
The court that granted the extension was also competent to entertain applications for filing awards.
The extension was granted over the appellant’s objection.
issues.conclusion: The court had jurisdiction to entertain the award-related application and to extend the time for making the award.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Arbitration Act, 1940, the court competent to entertain applications for filing an award could extend the time for making it; the fact that the same court was handling a proceeding under the Succession Act did not deprive it of that jurisdiction.

predicates.arbitration_award_proceeding: The proceeding concerns an award made in an arbitration.
predicates.arbitrators_requested_more_time: The arbitrators applied to the court for additional time to make the award.
predicates.court_competent_to_entertain_award_filin: The court receiving the request was competent to entertain applications for filing awards.

issues.definition: When arbitrators request more time in an arbitration proceeding from a court competent to entertain award filings, that court may extend the time to make the award.

issues.legal_issue: A person whose appointment as executor and entitlement to property under a will depend on adoption is not yet an executor before adoption and may enter an arbitration agreement concerning the dispute.
material_facts: The will made the appellant executor and entitled him to the testator’s property only if the appellant was adopted by the testator or the widow.
The appellant had not been adopted when the arbitration agreement was made.
The appellant entered the arbitration agreement concerning the parties’ rights in the estate.
issues.conclusion: The appellant was not constituted an executor before adoption and could enter into the arbitration agreement.
issues.legal_principle: On the construction of the will, the appellant would become executor and obtain the relevant property only upon adoption; section 301 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925, concerning renunciation or discharge did not arise because he had not yet become executor.

predicates.arbitration_proceeding: The dispute is referred to arbitration.
predicates.will_makes_executor_status_conditional_o: The will makes a person’s status as executor dependent on that person being adopted.
predicates.adoption_not_yet_occurred: The adoption on which executor status depends had not occurred when the arbitration agreement was made.

issues.definition: When a will makes executor status conditional on adoption and adoption has not occurred, the conditional appointee may enter an arbitration agreement before adoption.

issues.legal_issue: An arbitrator’s conduct does not establish misconduct where the evidence shows an attempt to secure an amicable settlement and does not prove that the arbitrators prejudged the dispute.
material_facts: The appellant alleged that the arbitrators had decided on an award before hearing the parties.
The allegation was not included in the appellant’s first application of objections.
The other arbitrators explained that they had sought an amicable settlement and requested more time after the parties did not meet with them as expected.
The High Court found that misconduct had not been proved.
issues.conclusion: The charge of misconduct was not proved, and no inference of misconduct could be drawn from the evidence described.
issues.legal_principle: The evidence of an effort to bring about an amicable settlement and an application for more time did not establish that the arbitrators had prejudged the matter; the unproved allegation did not establish misconduct.

predicates.arbitration_award_challenge: A party challenged an award in an arbitration proceeding on the ground of arbitrator misconduct.
predicates.alleged_prejudgment_not_proved: The evidence did not prove that the arbitrators had decided the award before hearing the parties.
predicates.arbitrators_sought_amicable_settlement: The arbitrators attempted to bring the parties to an amicable settlement and sought additional time when that effort did not proceed as expected.

issues.definition: When a challenge alleges prejudgment but does not prove it, and the arbitrators’ conduct is consistent with seeking settlement, misconduct is not established.

issues.legal_issue: An award is within the arbitrators’ authority when the agreement refers the consequences of adoption or non-adoption to them, including the consequences of either party’s default and a time limit needed to resolve the matter.
material_facts: The arbitration agreement specifically directed the arbitrators to decide the consequences of adoption or non-adoption and the parties’ respective rights if adoption occurred.
The will entitled the appellant to the property only if he was adopted.
The award set a time limit for adoption and provided different consequences depending on which party defaulted.
The award maintained the gifts made by the will and required the property owner to provide for the named persons and charities.
issues.conclusion: The arbitrators acted within the authority conferred by the agreement; the time limit was implicit in the reference, and the award did not disregard the will’s gifts.
issues.legal_principle: The scope of the arbitrators’ authority is determined by the arbitration agreement. Where the agreement assigns the consequences of adoption and non-adoption to the arbitrators, a time limit may be implicit because the relevant events cannot be left open indefinitely. The award also had to be read consistently with the will’s conditional grant and preserved gifts.

rule.if: arbitration_award_challenge and agreement_assigns_adoption_consequences_to_arbitrators and adoption_required_for_claimed_property and award_distinguishes_each_party_default

predicates.arbitration_award_challenge: A party challenged an award in an arbitration proceeding as exceeding the arbitrators’ authority.
predicates.agreement_assigns_adoption_consequences_: The arbitration agreement directs the arbitrators to decide the consequences of adoption or non-adoption.
predicates.adoption_required_for_claimed_property: The person claiming the relevant property would receive it only if adoption occurred.
predicates.award_distinguishes_each_party_default: The award assigns different consequences depending on which party prevents adoption from occurring.

issues.definition: When an arbitration agreement assigns adoption consequences to the arbitrators, property entitlement depends on adoption, and the award addresses each party’s default, the award is within the authority conferred by the agreement.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge based on the alleged failure to carry out a conditional adoption does not arise where the appellant was not prepared to accept the adoption.
material_facts: The award made the parties’ rights depend on whether adoption occurred and provided consequences if either party defaulted.
The courts below found that the appellant was not prepared to be adopted.
The Supreme Court reviewed the evidence and found no reason to differ from that finding.
issues.conclusion: Because the appellant was not prepared to be adopted, the alternative argument about considering subsequent events did not arise.
issues.legal_principle: Where the factual finding is that the appellant was unwilling to accept the adoption, the challenge based on the other party’s alleged failure to complete adoption, and on later events, does not arise.

predicates.appeal_from_decree_on_arbitral_award: The proceeding is an appeal from a decree given in terms of an arbitral award.
predicates.award_makes_rights_conditional_on_adopti: The award makes the parties’ rights depend on whether an adoption occurs.
predicates.appellant_not_prepared_to_accept_adoptio: The appellant was not prepared to accept the adoption contemplated by the award.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a decree on an award whose consequences depend on adoption, if the appellant was not prepared to accept adoption, a challenge relying on subsequent events does not arise.

issues.legal_issue: An award does not pervert the line of succession merely by providing that a share received by the widow will form her separate property.
material_facts: The will made the appellant’s entitlement to the testator’s property conditional on adoption.
The award provided that, if adoption took place, the widow would receive a share of the property and that the share would form her stridhan.
The appellant argued that this arrangement perverted the line of succession.
issues.conclusion: The award did not pervert the line of succession by providing that the widow’s share would form her stridhan.
issues.legal_principle: The award’s provision that the widow would receive a share if adoption occurred and that it would form her stridhan did not, without more, pervert the line of succession.

predicates.arbitration_award_challenge: A party challenged an award in an arbitration proceeding as affecting the line of succession.
predicates.award_conditionally_allocates_share_to_w: The award gives a widow a share of the estate if a specified adoption occurs.
predicates.award_makes_share_her_separate_property: The award provides that the widow’s share will be her separate property.

issues.definition: When an award conditionally gives a widow a share and makes it her separate property, that allocation alone does not pervert succession.
